"The Italian Prime Minister welcomes the agreement with Trump on Ukraine at the G7 summit": Meloni proposed to appoint a single EU negotiator on Ukraine.

"Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni intends to propose at the EU summit in Brussels the appointment of a single EU representative for negotiations with Russia on Ukraine. According to her, the candidate should be from a "medium-sized" country, not from among the largest states, so as not to complicate the achievement of consensus. Meloni also stated that the G7 leaders in Evian managed to agree on a position on Ukraine with Donald Trump - and this "cannot always be taken for granted".

Meloni advocates the appointment of a single negotiator, as the multiplicity of diplomatic formats within the EU creates confusion and weakens Europe's positions. She will raise this issue at the meeting of heads of state and government of the EU, which will take place in Brussels on June 18-19. Among the possible candidates were previously named former German Chancellors Angela Merkel and Gerhard Schröder, as well as former Italian Prime Minister Mario Draghi. However, Meloni, apparently, believes that the figure should be less obvious."

A House divided: Trump’s top advisers clash over Iran agreement 

Even some of President Trump's closest allies are turning against his Iran deal.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe told Trump that U.S. intelligence doubts Iran will follow through on its nuclear commitments. 
"The intelligence reflects that the Iranian intentions are not in line with their commitments under the deal,"
 according to a source within the CIA. 

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have also raised concerns in internal meetings, questioning whether Iran will accept the nuclear terms the U.S. wants.

Critics say the deal gives away too much. Iran gets oil exports, billions in frozen assets, and a $300 billion reconstruction fund — while offering only vague promises on its nuclear program. Conservative commentator Marc Thiessen called it "a disaster."

The full text hasn't been released yet, and even loyalists like Sen. Lindsey Graham and Fox's Mark Levin are demanding to see it.

The administration is split: Vance, Witkoff, and Kushner pushed the deal forward, while Ratcliffe, Rubio, and Hegseth opposed it. Knowing Trump, he might consider purging the dissenters.
